# ssp_telemetry_config (Resource)

Manages the SSP telemetry (CEIP) configuration.

This is a singleton resource — only one telemetry configuration exists per SSP platform.
Use `terraform import ssp_telemetry_config.this singleton` to adopt the existing configuration.

Corresponds to `GET/PUT /ssp/telemetry/config`.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `ceip_acceptance` (Boolean) When `true`, product usage data is collected and shared with VMware by Broadcom as part of the Customer Experience Improvement Programme (CEIP).
- `telemetry_agreement_displayed` (Boolean) Whether the CEIP agreement dialog has been displayed to the user.

### Optional

- `telemetry_schedule` (Attributes) Schedule controlling when telemetry data is uploaded. If omitted, the platform default (`WEEKLY_TELEMETRY_SCHEDULE` on `SUNDAY` at `02:00`) is used. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--telemetry_schedule))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Always `singleton` for this resource.
- `telemetry_collector_instance_id` (String) Read-only telemetry collector instance ID assigned by the platform.

<a id="nestedatt--telemetry_schedule"></a>

### Nested Schema for `telemetry_schedule`

Optional:

- `day_of_month` (Number) Day of the month (1-31) the telemetry upload runs. Only applicable when `frequency_type` is `MONTHLY_TELEMETRY_SCHEDULE`. Defaults to `1`.
- `day_of_week` (String) Day of the week the telemetry upload runs. Only applicable when `frequency_type` is `WEEKLY_TELEMETRY_SCHEDULE`. Defaults to `SUNDAY`.
- `frequency_type` (String) Telemetry upload frequency. One of `DAILY_TELEMETRY_SCHEDULE` (requires `hour_of_day`/`minutes`), `WEEKLY_TELEMETRY_SCHEDULE` (requires `day_of_week`/`hour_of_day`/`minutes`), or `MONTHLY_TELEMETRY_SCHEDULE` (requires `day_of_month`/`hour_of_day`/`minutes`). Defaults to `WEEKLY_TELEMETRY_SCHEDULE`.
- `hour_of_day` (Number) Hour of day (0-23) the telemetry upload runs. Defaults to `2`.
- `minutes` (Number) Minute of the hour (0-59) the telemetry upload runs. Defaults to `0`.
